page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-8xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 8 shared vCPUs and 8 physical cores operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals distinct performance tradeoffs. The shared CPU allocation results in poor single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 772.79, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested servers. However, multi-core performance is average, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 6254.7 and a PassMark CPU score of 15650.13. Memory performance is mixed; while cached read bandwidth is average at 821.2 GB/sec, the PassMark memory score is weak, landing in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput is also weak at 6.02 GB/sec. For LLM workloads, prompt processing and text generation are average for small 135M models but drop to weak and poor tiers for medium 7B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server leverages shared CPU resources and a lack of bundled local storage to offer a budget-friendly profile for multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core performance. It is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, multi-threaded decompression tasks, Redis key-value stores processing up to 11.84 million SET operations per second, and moderate database operations.
